common_name: Sugar Plum Heuchera (Metallic Silver-Overlay Purple-Pink Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic to neutral soil in partial shade.

directions: Plant in partial shade to light shade in well-drained, humus-rich soil, providing afternoon shade protection in hot climates. Sugar Plum bears rounded, ruffled leaves in a rich purple-pink base color overlaid with a metallic silver sheen that catches the light and shifts tone through the day, giving the foliage more visual depth than a flat single-color cultivar. Sprays of small, airy pink-white flowers rise on thin wiry stems above the foliage in late spring, attracting hummingbirds and small pollinators. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring, replanting slightly deeper than the original position as the crown lifts over time.

Mahogany is a long-established coral bells cultivar bearing smooth, glossy, dark reddish-brown leaves that hold their deep color reliably through the growing season, an early entry in the dark-foliage heuchera breeding line that later gave rise to near-black cultivars like Obsidian and Black Taffeta. common_name: Tiramisu Heuchera (Chartreuse-Gold Coral Bells with Red-Purple Undersides)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or early fall in well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic to neutral soil in partial shade.

directions: Plant in partial shade to light shade in well-drained, humus-rich soil, providing afternoon shade protection in hot climates. Tiramisu bears bright chartreuse-gold foliage on top with a contrasting red-purple underside and petiole that flashes through when a breeze lifts the leaves, adding a hidden layer of color to what would otherwise be a straightforward gold-leaved cultivar. Sprays of small, airy cream flowers rise on thin wiry stems above the foliage in late spring. The bright gold top color holds up well with a bit of morning sun but can scorch in strong afternoon exposure, so afternoon shade is important in hot climates. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring, replanting slightly deeper than the original position as the crown lifts over time.
